name: Light-aged
describes: Light, ultraviolet above all, photo-oxidises the lignin and extractives in a thin surface layer of wood, forming coloured carbonyl compounds: pale woods yellow and darken, dark extractive-rich woods can lighten. The change starts at once and is fastest at first; a clear finish slows it but does not stop it. Its signature is a sharp-edged difference where something has shaded the wood: under a rug, a frame or an object on a table.

mechanism.text: Photo-oxidation or photochemical degradation affects only the wood surface and starts immediately after exposure; solar radiation depolymerises lignin and cellulose; colour change is the main indicator.
mechanism.source: Teacă, C.-A., Roşu, D., Bodîrlău, R. & Roşu, L. (2013) Structural changes in wood under artificial UV light irradiation determined by FTIR spectroscopy and color measurements - a brief review. BioResources 8(1), 1478-1507, https://bioresources.cnr.ncsu.edu/resources/structural-changes-in-wood-under-artificial-uv-light-irradiation-determined-by-ftir-spectroscopy-and-color-measurements-a-brief-review/

fumedOak.text: Ammonia-fumed oak had better colour resistance against UV than heat-treated oak; fuming can pre-age wood and stabilise its colour.
fumedOak.source: Miklečić, J., Španić, N. & Jirouš-Rajković, V. (2012) Wood color changes by ammonia fuming. BioResources 7(3), 3767-3778, https://bioresources.cnr.ncsu.edu/resources/wood-color-changes-by-ammonia-fuming/

museumLight.text: UV kept below 75 uW/lm (about 10 uW/lm for the most sensitive), light by use; direct sun patches are part of the Salon's design (bay 1 and bay 5 cross the oak).
museumLight.source: Michalski, S. (2018) Agent of deterioration: light, ultraviolet and infrared. Canadian Conservation Institute, 2018-05-17, https://www.canada.ca/en/conservation-institute/services/agents-deterioration/light.html ; plan/proposals/salon-interior/canvas/Light.dc.html (approved Salon interior proposal)

terms.shadowLine: Where a piece is shaded (under a case's plinth, behind a frame, under a bench's footprint) the unaged tone keeps a crisp edge.

up: daylight and UV on the piece (Light's dose at the surface)

photograph: A warmer, more golden tone on sunlit oak than on the same boards in shade; paler rectangles where something stood.

unverified.reason: Search summaries report that about half of oak's colour change under UV occurs in the first 20 hours and give delta E of about 4-6 under visible and UV lamps; the papers could not be opened.
